attested.notes: Four rounds of stranger read with a real outside reader, in persona, rather than an override. The reader found things I could not see. Round 1: the opening I was pleased with was the worst part, because it talked about our research process rather than his problem, and he nearly closed the tab at sentence one. Round 2: I had written 'it takes one call' when it takes days, which was simply untrue, and there was nothing he could do that night. Round 3: Barclays, the only lender that can refuse him, was seven paragraphs down, and the page never addressed the thing keeping him awake, which was that his application had already gone in with a possibly wrong answer. Round 4: the page assumed he knew he had a judgment, when he had an unexplained letter, and a name-and-address search could return a false clear. Every one of those is now fixed. Added: how to tell a judgment from a claim form or a demand, what to type into the register search and why a wrong address gives a meaningless nil result, the six pound fee rather than 'a small fee', the personal guarantee check that breaks the page's whole premise, plain wording on offer withdrawal and mortgage fraud, and a gloss on winding-up petition. Vocabulary standardised on paid and satisfied. Reader's closing verdict on round 4: 'That's a plan. First time I've had one.'
